t: This is Nunhead Cemetery in Southwark, one of London's Magnificent Seven cemeteries, and perhaps the least famous of them. It was consecrated in 1840 and first called All Saints' Cemetery. Today it's a local nature reserve. Among those buried here is Bryan Donkin, the engineer who developed the first paper making machine and the world's first commercial canning factory. Frederick Abel, who invented cordite, lies here too. So does the Egyptologist E. A. Wallis Budge, who worked for the British Museum. The astronomer and mathematician Thomas Harriot is also buried here.
